【141†(macOS) Transparent Titlebar with Custom Window Background Color】 L191: # Window Customization L192: L193: Tauri provides lots of options for customizing the look and feel of your app’s window. You can create custom titlebars, have transparent windows, enforce size constraints, and more. L194: L195: ## Configuration L196: L197: 【130†Section titled “Configuration”】 L198: L199: There are three ways to change the window configuration: L200: L201: * 【142†Through tauri.conf.json】 L202: * 【143†Through the JavaScript API】 L203: * 【144†Through the Window in Rust†docs.rs】 L204: ## Usage L205: L206: 【131†Section titled “Usage”】 L207: L208: * 【132†Creating a Custom Titlebar】 L209: * 【141†(macOS) Transparent Titlebar with Custom Window Background Color】 L210: ### Creating a Custom Titlebar L211: L212: 【132†Section titled “Creating a Custom Titlebar”】 L213: L214: A common use of these window features is creating a custom titlebar. This short tutorial will guide you through that process. L215: L216: Note L217: For macOS, using a custom titlebar will also lose some features provided by the system, such as 【145†moving or aligning the window†support.apple.com】. Another approach to customizing the titlebar but keeping native functions could be making the titlebar transparent and setting the window background color. See the usage 【141†(macOS) Transparent Titlebar with Custom Window Background Color】. L218: #### tauri.conf.json L219: L220: 【133†Section titled “tauri.conf.json”】 L221: L222: Set `decorations` to `false` in your `tauri.conf.json`: L223: L224: tauri.conf.json L225: L226: ` L227: L228: "tauri": { L229: L230: "windows": [ L231: L232: { L233: L234: "decorations": false L235: L236: } L237: L238: ] L239: L240: } L241: L242: ` L243: #### Permissions L244: L245: 【134†Section titled “Permissions”】 L246: L247: Add window permissions in capability file. L248: L249: By default, all plugin commands are blocked and cannot be accessed. You must define a list of permissions in your `capabilities` configuration. L250: L251: See the 【29†Capabilities Overview】 for more information and the 【89†step by step guide】 to use plugin permissions. L252: src-tauri/capabilities/default.json L253: L254: ` L255: L256: { L257: L258: "$schema": "../gen/schemas/desktop-schema.json", L259: L260: "identifier": "main-capability", L261: L262: "description": "Capability for the main window", L263: L264: "windows": ["main"], L265: L266: "permissions": [ L267: L268: "core:window:default", L269: L270: "core:window:allow-close", L271: L272: "core:window:allow-minimize", L273: L274: "core:window:allow-toggle-maximize", L275: L276: "core:window:allow-start-dragging" L277: L278: ] L279: L280: } L281: L282: ` L283: Permission | Description L284: --- | --- L285: `core:window:default` | Default permissions for the plugin. This includes `core:window:allow-internal-toggle-maximize`. L286: `core:window:allow-close` | Enables the close command without any pre-configured scope. L287: `core:window:allow-minimize` | Enables the minimize command without any pre-configured scope. L288: `core:window:allow-start-dragging` | Enables the start_dragging command without any pre-configured scope. L289: `core:window:allow-toggle-maximize` | Enables the toggle_maximize command without any pre-configured scope. L290: `core:window:allow-internal-toggle-maximize` | Enables the internal_toggle_maximize command without any pre-configured scope. L291: #### CSS L292: L293: 【135†Section titled “CSS”】 L294: Add this CSS sample to keep it at the top of the screen and style the buttons: L295: L296: ` L297: L298: .titlebar { L299: L300: height: 30 px; L301: L302: background: #329ea3; L303: L304: user-select: none; L305: L306: display: grid; L307: L308: grid-template-columns: auto max-content; L309: L310: position: fixed; L311: L312: top: 0; L313: L314: left: 0; L315: L316: right: 0; L317: L318: } L319: L320: .titlebar > .controls { L321: L322: display: flex; L323: L324: } L325: L326: .titlebar button { L327: L328: appearance: none; L329: padding: 0; L330: L331: margin: 0; L332: L333: border: none; L334: L335: display: inline-flex; L336: L337: justify-content: center; L338: L339: align-items: center; L340: L341: width: 30 px; L342: L343: background-color: transparent; L344: L345: } L346: L347: .titlebar button:hover { L348: L349: background: #5bbec3; L350: L351: } L352: L353: ` L354: #### HTML L355: L356: 【136†Section titled “HTML”】 L357: Put this at the top of your `` tag: L358: L359: ` L360: L361:
